title: Demystifying Git
description:
**Topic**
Many of us use git for our day to day work, but do we really know whats going on? Today we will peek under the hood and get an idea of how git works under the covers. By understanding some of the git internals, we will be better equipped to recover when things go wrong (hello merge hell). No matter if you’re a beginner or an expert, there will be something you can use to improve your workflow.

**Agenda**
5:30 - Start of pizza and networking
6:00 - Demystifying Git
7:15 - Finish

Please make sure to register for the event as we need to provide contact details to Microsoft for security purposes. Registration will close 48 hours prior to the event to provide enough time to send out the access passes for in-person attendees, but you can [join online](https://aka.ms/aotearoanzgithub/stream) on the day.

If you have a topic you'd like to present (or hear about) please reach out, or create an idea in our [GitHub Ideas discussion board](https://github.com/orgs/NZ-GitHub-UG/discussions/categories/ideas).

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please use the following link to pre-register for Xero Venue before arriving** [https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/myweaHurOU55lj2S](https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/myweaHurOU55lj2S).
* **Organisers will be at the building entrance to bring everyone to the venue.**
* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: Shipping software as a Junior without burning out by Enry Villamizar**
Stepping into software engineering is exciting, but navigating the steep learning curve alongside deliverable deadlines can easily lead to early-career fatigue. In this talk, you will learn actionable strategies for shipping production-ready code confidently without sacrificing well-being. From setting clear boundaries and managing workload expectations to building sustainable dev habits.

**A bit about Enry:**

* Enry is a Senior Software Developer driven by solving real-world business problems through smart internal software, such as building Whites Powersports’ warehouse system and Wireless Nation’s dashboard. A huge fan of video games and AI, he cares deeply about keeping development work sustainable, efficient, and burnout-free.

**Talk 2: Beyond the Prompt: Becoming a Better Developer in the Age of AI by Keith Patton**
AI tools can help junior developers produce working code faster than ever, but speed is not the same as engineering competence.
In this talk, he will share practical lessons from using AI coding tools and agentic development workflows in real software teams. He will cover where AI is genuinely useful, where it can create false confidence, and how developers can use it without outsourcing their understanding or judgement.

title: Build Night: Demos, Collabs & Open Source in Practice
description:
A fortnightly, hands-on session focused on the projects the Auckland AI Collective is actually building — together.

Each session centres on **demonstrations** of what members are working on. Expect live demos, group experiments, and the occasional "let's just try it and see what happens" moment — so come ready to get involved, not just watch. Some parts may invite your participation; none of it is polished or precious.

The tone is **casual and informal**\- eat dinner\, drink\, and enjoy\. This is a place to share ideas\, get feedback\, find collaborators\, and turn "someone should build that" into an actual repo\.

What we cover will vary week to week depending on what people bring and what the group is curious about — the constant is the room: builders comparing notes and starting things together.

**This is for you if** you want to get directly and personally involved in group projects, collaborations, and **open source**.

See what we're already building on GitHub: [https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective](https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective)

Bring a project, a problem, an idea, or just yourself.

After this session we can hang out as long as we like at the restaurant if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Keeping the Customer in the Room: How Trade Me Is Rewiring Product Work
description:
AI is rewriting the rules of product development, but what happens to the customer when everything moves faster? Trade Me will pull back the curtain on the new ways of working they're trialing to keep pace with AI without losing sight of the people they build for. Building both consumer-facing AI products and more traditional ones with the help of AI tools has opened up huge opportunities, but also thrown up real challenges across product, design and research. Come hear how their teams are navigating that tension — and what they're learning along the way.

**FYI this is a free event** \- you do not need a meetup subscription to RSVP/attend\! So you can click past the upsell dialogs that you'll possibly get when RSVPing\.

**Note that the livestream will kick off from just before 6pm!**

**About our speakers:**
**[Sue Anderson](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sueanderson/)** \- Head of Product and Marketing \- Trade Me Marketplace
Sue leads marketing & product vision and strategy for our buyers and sellers. Sue doesn't claim to have all the answers — she'd rather spend time in the uncomfortable problem space, figuring out the right customer problem to solve before jumping to solutions.

**[Liz Miller](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lizcashen/)** is Head of Product for Trade Me Property, looking after B2C products for property buyers and homeowners. She also leads the Research Operations and SEO teams, and is driving Trade Me's consumer-facing AI product work. Liz has worked in digital and product for over 15 years, with a passion for developing and coaching other product people.

**[Brandon Johnston](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brandonjjohnston/)** \- Principal Product Designer \- Trade Me Property

title: The Great Beauty (Italy 2013, 2 hrs 20 mins)
description:
A Great Beauty is a character study which presents the City of Rome through the eyes of Jep, a charming, smug writer who, apart from one novella written long ago, never writes anything. Jep is brilliant, witty and perceptive and infuriating. He has spent his life charming the celebrities and literati of Rome, and working the nightlife scene of the city.

However, as he turns 65, he starts to take stock of his life turning his cutting wit on himself and his contemporaries, and looking past the lavish nightclubs, parties, and cafés to find Rome itself, in all its monumental glory: a timeless landscape of absurd, exquisite beauty."
(The Criterion Collection)

The film is beautifully filmed and won the Academy Award for Best International Feature. A must see for those devoted to good film making.
